title: Slice test cell: skill body budget and reference integrity
action: The consolidated test cell for this slice, per the rule fs-1 shipped. The slice's net behavior is instruction text - three rules moved into references with routing lines left in the bodies - so what is mechanically testable is the two properties that make the thin-body doctrine real, plus the ordered-list integrity that moving steps around breaks. All three were violated at least once while authoring this very slice, which is why they earn a suite rather than a promise. scripts/tests/test_skill_body_budget.mjs asserts: a per-skill body byte budget as a RATCHET (recorded baseline, may only shrink; --update-baseline lowers, never raises), that every flow-batch-2 body stayed at or below its pre-slice size, that every references/<file>.md ("Heading") pointer in any body resolves to a real file and a real heading (same-skill or cross-skill), that the three moved rules are reachable from a body pointer, that bee-validating routes to the merged reviewer prompt while the retired split prompts are gone and all four finding classes survive, and that no body repeats a number within one ordered list. This also lands spec #78 P2's byte-budget fence as a ratchet rather than an absolute cap.

truths: Every check is falsifiable: growing a body, breaking an anchor, and duplicating a step number each fail the intended check and only that check.
The baseline is a ratchet - --update-baseline lowers a budget but never raises one.
Cross-skill pointers (bee-hive/references/...) resolve, not just same-skill ones.
The suite is registered in the impact registry and runs in the full verify.
prohibitions: Do NOT raise a recorded budget to make a body fit.
Do NOT weaken a check to accommodate a body that grew.

verify: node scripts/tests/test_skill_body_budget.mjs && node scripts/ledger_parity.mjs --check && node scripts/release_manifest.mjs --check && node scripts/run_verify.mjs
